class.name: AudioStreamOpus
class.brief_description: A class representing an Opus audio stream.
class.description: The AudioStreamOpus class is a specialized [AudioStream] for handling Opus file formats. It offers functionality for loading and playing back Opus files, as well as managing looping and other playback properties. More info can be found in [ResourceImporterOpus]. [b]Runtime loading:[/b] Opus files without an import (for example in [code]user://[/code], in a mod folder, at an absolute path or in a PCK as raw files) are loaded with [method ResourceLoader.load] as [AudioStreamOpus], with the resource cache, [method ResourceLoader.load_threaded_request] and [method ResourceLoader.exists]. They use the default import options ([member loop] off, no [member bpm]); set the properties after loading if needed. The data stays compressed and is decoded while playing. Files that are not valid Ogg Opus data fail to load with [constant ERR_FILE_CORRUPT]. Opus files under [code]res://[/code] that have a [code].import[/code] file are still loaded through their importer, unless the import mode is "Keep File" or "Skip File". [b]Note:[/b] [method ResourceSaver.save] cannot write [code].opus[/code] files, because the engine has no Opus encoder. Save the stream as [code].tres[/code] or [code].res[/code] instead. [codeblocks] [gdscript] var voice = ResourceLoader.load("user://voices/greeting.opus") as AudioStreamOpus voice.loop = false $AudioStreamPlayer.stream = voice $AudioStreamPlayer.play() [/gdscript] [csharp] var voice = ResourceLoader.Load<AudioStreamOpus>("user://voices/greeting.opus"); voice.Loop = false; GetNode<AudioStreamPlayer>("AudioStreamPlayer").Stream = voice; GetNode<AudioStreamPlayer>("AudioStreamPlayer").Play(); [/csharp] [/codeblocks]

method.name: load_from_buffer
method.description: Creates a new [AudioStreamOpus] instance from the given buffer. The buffer must contain Opus data.

method.name: load_from_file
method.description: Creates a new [AudioStreamOpus] instance from the given file path. The file must be in Opus format.

members.member: The number of beats within a single bar in the audio track.

The length of the audio track, in beats. The actual duration of the audio file might be longer than what is indicated by this property. It defines the end of the audio for looping, [AudioStreamPlaylist], and [AudioStreamInteractive].
The tempo of the audio track, measured in beats per minute.
Contains the raw Opus data for this stream.

If [code]true[/code], the stream will play again from the specified [member loop_offset] once it reaches the end of the audio track, or once it reaches the end of the last beat according to the amount specified in [member beat_count]. Useful for ambient sounds and background music.
Time in seconds at which the stream starts after being looped.

Contains user-defined tags if found in the Opus data. Commonly used tags include [code]title[/code], [code]artist[/code], [code]album[/code], [code]tracknumber[/code], and [code]date[/code] ([code]date[/code] does not have a standard date format). [b]Note:[/b] No tag is [i]guaranteed[/i] to be present in every file, so make sure to account for the keys not always existing.
